purpose: Map of lifecycle phases and their skills, model tiers, and instructions; what is being built (project) versus the AI-SDLC tooling (process); and the files that need a human's review. Each review-gated file and template also says so in its own first lines.

review_gated.rule: Edit only with a human's explicit approval; changes need a code owner's review (.github/CODEOWNERS).

fix.meaning: Makes behaviour match an existing spec or decision.
fix.test: Does a spec already say this is how it should behave?

refactor.test: Do all existing tests pass unchanged?
refactor.workflow: Tests unchanged and green; remove duplication.

docs.test: Would every rule, value and decision read the same afterwards?

tooling.meaning: Tooling and process, no product behaviour.
tooling.test: Does the app behave the same?
tooling.workflow: Run the checks; review closely if review-gated paths are touched.

feat.meaning: Adds behaviour or a new versioned ruleset, keeping existing decisions.
feat.test: Does anything that already exists change meaning?
feat.workflow: Spec, tests and code together in one change.

BREAKING.meaning: After any prefix, changes or removes a decision others depend on.
BREAKING.test: Does it supersede or retire anything?
BREAKING.workflow: Change record (supersedes, retires), ripple, code in the same change.

review.meaning: Records a human review via scripts/sdlc.py, no file changes.
review.test: Were the changes checked by a human?

templates.rule: Copy to a new numbered file; never fill in the template itself.
